contract: infer_fluxes(network, atom_maps, training_measurements, training_objective, budget) -> {fluxes,intervals}. network includes stoichiometry, bounds, feasible_initial_fluxes. Enforce S@v tolerance1e-6 and flux bounds. Trusted source-specific isotope simulator produces held-out Gaussian NLL. intervals nflux x2 must contain estimates. Forward-model source/hash required; no synthetic fallback.
notes: Independently written bounded scientific adaptation. Source data and SHA256 preparation receipts required. See docs/BIOLOGY_EXPANSION.md and task limitations; fixture tests never establish source benchmark reproduction.

name: Biology: Isotope-constrained metabolic flux inference
description: Infer steady-state reaction fluxes and uncertainty intervals from isotope measurements using a verified source-specific atom-mapping forward model.
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Theorell et al. model/likelihood formulation, metabolic flux posterior inference; Supplementary Data1 model files.
Official author implementation/data reference; evaluator and seed are independently written, not copied.

limitations: Source FML atom-map models require a verified isotope simulator port; generic linear surrogates are not substituted. Adapter enforces flux constraints and held-out likelihood but interval calibration requires separate known-flux experiments.
Public source subsets are development-visible. Freeze candidates before evaluating on additional independently chosen studies/instances; trusted candidate execution is not a security sandbox.
Improving this benchmark is a scientific-method result; it does not alone establish a new biological discovery.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Infer intracellular metabolic reaction rates and uncertainty from isotope-labeling observations.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Metabolic fluxes describe how cells process nutrients and support quantitative understanding of metabolism.

papers.title: BayFlux: A Bayesian method to quantify metabolic Fluxes and their uncertainty at the genome scale
papers.primary_goal: Infer probability distributions of metabolic fluxes consistent with experimental isotope and physiological measurements.
papers.task_relation: BayFlux directly solves isotope-constrained flux inference with uncertainty. The local task uses a separately specified atom-mapping model and source measurements; its restricted steady-state network and intervals do not reproduce the paper's genome-scale experiments.

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
